page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at 3.2 GHz. The configuration provides 24 dedicated physical cores and 24 vCPUs, operating with a single thread per core. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage options.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.cm4.6xlarge in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. In CPU testing, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1575.18 and a multi-core score of 24949.83, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 9204.0. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 1392.19 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 96.09 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Database operations, measured via Redis SET, reached 23.45 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput registered at 14.7 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the instance processed 1344.67 prompt tokens per second using a small 135M model, though performance drops to 35.12 tokens per second for a medium 7B model.

The hardware profile offers a balanced resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. However, the lack of local storage and GPU accelerators represents a clear tradeoff, limiting its utility for large-scale data storage or heavy deep learning training. The instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including software compilation, text and image processing, web serving, and moderate database operations.
